blocks.text: SHEMAIAH, “THE MAN OF GOD”, IN THE DAYS OF REHOBOAM · TWO KINGDOMS
Shemaiah. He stopped a war between brothers, and told Rehoboam's princes why Shishak had come.
SCRIPTURE CALLS
Prophet
ERA
Two kingdoms 930–586 BC
IN THE DAYS OF
Rehoboam
BOOK
None bears the name
HOW THE WORD CAME
“The word of God came unto Shemaiah the man of God, saying, Speak unto Rehoboam”; Chronicles has “the word of the LORD”.
THE CALL
How the word came
“The word of God came unto Shemaiah the man of God, saying, Speak unto Rehoboam”; Chronicles has “the word of the LORD”. 1 Kings 12:22–23 2 Chronicles 11:2
After the princes humbled themselves, “the word of the LORD came to Shemaiah” a second time. 2 Chronicles 12:7
Chronicles names “the book of Shemaiah the prophet” for the acts of Rehoboam. 2 Chronicles 12:15
BEFORE THE KINGS
Before Rehoboam
KING OF JUDAH
Rehoboam
“Thus saith the LORD, Ye have forsaken me, and therefore have I also left you in the hand of Shishak.”
2 Chronicles 12:5 (KJV) →
THE MESSAGE
The word in its main themes
Do not fight your brothers
“Ye shall not go up, nor fight against your brethren the children of Israel: return every man to his house; for this thing is from me.”
1 Kings 12:24 (KJV) →
Forsaken, and left to Shishak
Humbled, and given some deliverance
“They have humbled themselves; therefore I will not destroy them, but I will grant them some deliverance”
2 Chronicles 12:7 (KJV) →
THE WORD TO …
To whom the word was spoken
TO REHOBOAM AND THE HOUSE OF JUDAH AND BENJAMIN
“Ye shall not go up, nor fight against your brethren the children of Israel”
1 Kings 12:24 (KJV) →
TO REHOBOAM AND THE PRINCES OF JUDAH, AT JERUSALEM
“Ye have forsaken me, and therefore have I also left you in the hand of Shishak.”
2 Chronicles 12:5 (KJV) →
Jerusalem · Where Rehoboam gathered his army, and where the princes gathered because of Shishak
COMPANIONS AND OPPONENTS
Who stood with him, and against him
Iddo the seer
HOW THE STORY ENDS
Scripture says, tradition says
SCRIPTURE SAYS
From the textScripture does not tell of Shemaiah's death. 2 Chronicles 12:15
TRADITION SAYS
No tradition is recorded here.
OPEN QUESTIONS
Where readers have differed
Kings and Chronicles tell it side by side
The texts

Kings tells Shishak's attack and the treasures he took without naming Shemaiah; Chronicles adds the prophet's word and the princes' humbling. Both books tell the stopped war in nearly the same words. 1 Kings 14:25–26 2 Chronicles 12:2–9 1 Kings 12:21–24 2 Chronicles 11:1–4
Chronicles drew on a prophetic record
E. G. Hirsch and W. H. Bennett, Jewish Encyclopedia (1903)

Chronicles itself names “the book of Shemaiah the prophet” for Rehoboam's acts; the Jewish Encyclopedia lists “The Words of Shemaiah the Prophet and of Iddo the Seer” among the Chronicler's sources. 2 Chronicles 12:15 [43]
IN SCRIPTURE
Every passage
CHAPTERS · 3
1 Kings 12 2 Chronicles 11 2 Chronicles 12
PASSAGES · 4
1 Kings 12:21–24 2 Chronicles 11:1–4 2 Chronicles 12:1–8 2 Chronicles 12:15
WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture gives no father or home for this Shemaiah.
Kings does not mention Shemaiah in its account of Shishak (1 Kings 14:25–28).
Kings says there was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam “all their days” (1 Kings 14:30) and does not explain how that fits the war Shemaiah stopped.
He is a different man from Shemaiah the Nehelamite (Jeremiah 29:24) and the Shemaiah of Nehemiah 6:10.
